title: Reverse an array 2
statement:
Given an array **nums** of **n** integers, return reverse of the array.

**Example 1:**

```
Input : nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
Output : [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input : nums = [1, 3, 3, 3, 5]
Output : [5, 3, 3, 3, 1]
```

peerSolutions.title: Python slicing gives a short reversed array result
peerSolutions.author: Neha Agarwal
peerSolutions.content:
This version creates the answer with Python slicing. A step of `-1` reads the list from the last index to the first, so the original list stays unchanged.

The empty list and a one-item list also work without any special condition.

```python
class Solution:
    def reverseArray(self, nums):
        return nums[::-1]
```

Time complexity: `O(n)`.

Space complexity: `O(n)` because slicing creates a new list.
